title: OpenBSD top(1) adds flag to show chroot, pledge and unveil status
excerpt: Contributed by Peter N. M. Hansteen on 2026-11-06 from the Q lifts the shroud dept.
content_html:
Contributed by Peter N. M. Hansteen on 2026-11-06 from the Q lifts the shroud dept.

With one recent commit, the top(1) command on OpenBSD became quite a bit more useful. The commit adds a new -Q flag to show each process' use of the chroot(2), pledge(2) and unveil(2) facilities.

The commit message reads, 

List:       openbsd-cvs
Subject:    CVS: cvs.openbsd.org: src
From:       Klemens Nanni <kn () cvs ! openbsd ! org>
Date:       2026-11-05 17:54:16

CVSROOT:	/cvs
Module name:	src
Changes by:	kn@cvs.openbsd.org	2026/11/05 11:54:16

Modified files:
	usr.bin/top    : display.c machine.c machine.h top.1 top.c 

Log message:
add Q flag/key to show pledge/chroot/unveil usage

Show promises in COMMAND and ps(1) state letters pertaining to pledge,
chroot and unveil usage in PRIV instead of TIME.

To quickly identify programs (un)aware of their privileges and thus
in extend the system's security.

A non-root user it not enough and alternatives like ps(1) -o state,pledge
in tree-mode or wrapped in watch(1) are not nearly as ergonomic as top(1).

p and P are already in use, Q has no meaning, but is free.

OK deraadt

You will need to install a fresh snapshot in order to explore and enjoy this feature.
